items.question: Who becomes free from bondage after six months of practice?
premises: six months of practice is prescribed
the practitioner becomes free from bondage
items.inference: six months of practice liberates from bondage
uncertainties: kāṣāyaṃ may denote ochre robe or ascetic state
items.plain_english: Whoever practices for six months becomes free from bondage, even while wearing the ochre robe.

items.question: Who is freed from all diseases and joins union with yogis?
premises: freedom from all diseases is attained
union with yogis follows
items.inference: liberation from disease leads to yogic fellowship
uncertainties: melakam may mean meeting or union
items.plain_english: Freed from all diseases, one attains union together with yogis.

items.question: What practice of the soul has been told to Bhairavi?
premises: the teaching is addressed to Bhairavi
the soul-practice has been declared
items.inference: Bhairavi receives the teaching of soul-practice
uncertainties: jīva+abhyāsa may mean living practice or soul practice
items.plain_english: This practice of the soul has been told to you, O Bhairavi.

items.question: To whom should the teaching be given?
premises: the recipient is endowed with all states
the recipient has a resolved mind
items.inference: the teaching is given to a fully endowed and resolved person
uncertainties: sarva+bhāva may mean all states or all beings
items.plain_english: It should be given to one endowed with all states and of resolved mind.

items.question: Should the kaula essence originating from yoginis be given?
premises: the kaula essence is not to be given
it originates from yoginis
items.inference: the kaula essence from yoginis is withheld
uncertainties: sambhavam may mean origin or arising
items.plain_english: The kaula essence originating from yoginis should not be given.

items.question: What has struck the pure body today?
premises: the body is pure
ignorance's veil has struck it
items.inference: ignorance veils the otherwise pure body
uncertainties: āhatam may mean struck or afflicted
items.plain_english: Today my pure body has been struck by the veil of ignorance.

items.question: What auspicious deception of time does the speaker wish to hear now?
premises: the speaker wishes to hear now
the topic is time's auspicious deception
items.inference: the speaker seeks knowledge of time's deception
uncertainties: vañcanaṃ may mean deception or cheating
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious deception of time.

items.question: How is death destroyed according to the teaching?
premises: the speaker tells without doubt
death is destroyed
items.inference: the teaching explains the destruction of death
uncertainties: yathā may introduce manner or comparison
items.plain_english: I tell you without doubt how death is destroyed.

items.question: What happens to even a wise person burning at the tip of nectar?
premises: burning occurs at the tip of nectar
even a wise person is affected
items.inference: nectar's tip burns even the wise
uncertainties: amṛta+agraṃ may mean tip of nectar or nectar's edge
items.plain_english: Even a wise person burns at the tip of nectar with the essence of juice.

items.question: How should air be drunk at the root of tongue and palate?
premises: air is placed at root of tongue and palate
it should be drunk slowly
items.inference: slow drinking of air at that root is prescribed
uncertainties: chanaiḥ may mean slowly or gently
items.plain_english: Having placed air at the root of tongue and palate, one should drink it slowly.

items.question: What is destroyed when the practice is done for one year?
premises: practice lasts one year
old age and death are destroyed
items.inference: one year of practice destroys old age and death
uncertainties: yadā+abhyastañ may mean when practiced or when repeated
items.plain_english: When practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: Does poison enter the body even when bitten by great serpents?
premises: poison does not enter the body
even a bite by great serpents is mentioned
items.inference: the body remains unaffected by poison and serpent bite
uncertainties: daṃśito may mean bitten or stung
items.plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one is bitten by great serpents.
